metadata.title: TALIS Teacher Knowledge Survey 2024 Conceptual and Assessment Framework (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a conceptual and assessment framework for the TALIS 2024 Teacher Knowledge Survey (TKS), not an empirical analysis of student-level outcomes. It specifies a two-stage sampling design for the eventual survey implementation: schools as primary sampling units and teachers as secondary sampling units, with systematic random school sampling and random teacher selection within schools, plus stratification where possible. The framework describes nominal sample sizes (about 200 schools and ~3,000 teachers per country) and provisions for excluding up to 5% of teachers in exceptional circumstances, but it does not report any applied student/sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures. For analyses using the eventual TALIS/TKS microdata, analysts should follow TALIS technical standards for complex survey design (school clustering and stratification) and apply the corresponding TALIS sampling weights; however, this specific framework document does not provide weight variable names or replication methods.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework and instrument-design document for the TALIS 2024 Teacher Knowledge Survey (TKS), not an empirical study estimating predictive models on cognitive outcomes. The TKS uses selected-response items for general pedagogical knowledge (GPK) and proposes scaling using Item Response Theory (IRT), but the document does not implement an analysis pipeline that would require plausible-value (PV) handling or a documented missing-data strategy. Missing-data handling is therefore not applicable to the reported content because no analytic dataset, imputation/deletion rules, or model estimation results are presented.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The document defines the target population and sampling approach for TALIS 2024 and the optional TKS module: teachers providing instruction at ISCED level 2 in participating countries/territories, excluding schools entirely devoted to special needs students and schools exclusively offering adult education. It specifies a two-stage design (schools sampled first, then teachers within schools) and notes that teachers are randomly selected within each school; in schools with 35+ eligible teachers, 15 teachers are selected for TKS. It also describes operational exclusions (e.g., up to 5% of teachers may be excluded if some schools cannot be surveyed) and replacement procedures for non-participating schools, but it does not provide an analytic dataset or country-by-country realized sample sizes for the framework itself.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD framework document articulates the conceptual basis and assessment design for the TALIS 2024 Teacher Knowledge Survey (TKS), an optional module of TALIS. The TKS targets teachers teaching at ISCED level 2 and measures teachers’ general pedagogical knowledge (GPK) across three dimensions—instruction, learning, and assessment—further divided into six sub-dimensions, with additional cross-cutting thematic orientations (core knowledge vs emergent priorities such as diversity, technology, social and emotional learning, and 21st century thinking skills). The instrument uses selected-response items only (simple and complex multiple choice) and is administered using a rotated block design: each teacher answers 39 of 52 total GPK items, enabling broader coverage without increasing completion time. Scaling is planned using IRT to derive measures of GPK at different knowledge levels. The document also specifies survey operational phases (pilot, field trial, main survey), timing, and sampling procedures, but it does not report empirical model performance or causal/predictive effects.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is intentionally sparse because the provided document is a conceptual and assessment framework (instrument design and validation rationale) rather than an empirical large-scale assessment analysis with reported model estimates. As a result, there is no analytic sample with country-level Ns, no implemented ML algorithm comparison, no PV-based outcome modeling, and no reported performance metrics. The framework nonetheless provides detailed guidance on the intended sampling design, item blueprinting, rotated block administration, and planned IRT scaling for the eventual TALIS 2024 TKS data collection.
